# Base-balanced moment bodies and the capacity-integration gap

This note adds an integer-base constraint to the fixed-mass moment
bodies in `candidate 9287833963d276a6`. The constraint
produces a genuine common convex body across continuous directions.
Its exact dual, curvature identity, and comparison with optimized
directional capacities are proved below. None asserts that this body
is contained in the OC depth region.

Let mu be the ordinary mixed d-volume of a bounded convex body in
R^n x R^d, n>=1 and d>=1. Retain only the finite positive-volume fibers P,
write w_z=|C_z|, M=sum w_z, and fix j in P. Put r_z=z-j.

## 1. The finite-base capacity and maximum balanced mass

Define the unnormalized integer halfspace capacity

 D_j=min{sum_(z in P intersect H) w_z:
                   H a closed integer-space halfspace containing j}.

For this finite base, the same minimum is obtained over the sets
{z:a.r_z>=-1}, a in R^n; the constant functional a=0 includes all P.
To see this, any minimizing halfspace can have its boundary moved
slightly away from j without changing its selected finite set, so that
j lies strictly inside, after which its threshold can be normalized
to -1. Conversely these normalized halfspaces all contain j. There
are finitely many selected subsets, so the minimum is attained.

Let

 T_max(j)=max{integral f dmu: 0<=f<=1,
                             integral (z-j)f dmu=0}.       (1)

This is the finite linear program in masses m_z=integral_(C_z) f:

 maximize sum_z m_z,
 0<=m_z<=w_z,  sum_z r_z m_z=0.

It has an attained optimum, and its elementary linear-program dual is

 T_max(j)=inf_a sum_z w_z(1+a.r_z)_+.                       (2)

The dual equality also follows from the separation argument in section
2, with no dependence on polyhedrality of the individual fibers.
For every a, Cavalieri gives

 sum_z w_z(1+a.r_z)_+
    =integral_0^infinity sum_(1+a.r_z>=s) w_z ds
    >=integral_0^1 D_j ds=D_j.                            (3)

Every level set in the last integral is a halfspace containing j;
the value at a single endpoint s=1 is immaterial. Therefore

 T_max(j)>=D_j.                                           (4)

In particular any t with 0<t<=D_j admits a dominated submeasure of
mass t whose integer centroid is j. This retains the full finite
integer geometry; it does not round a continuous centroid.

## 2. A common convex moment body and its exact dual

For 0<t<=T_max(j), define

 M_t(j)={t^(-1)integral x f(z,x)dmu:
            0<=f<=1, integral f=t, integral r_z f=0}.      (5)

It is nonempty, compact, and convex. Indeed the interval of functions
0<=f<=1 is weak-star compact in L-infinity(mu), and all its finitely
many mass and moment functionals are weak-star continuous because mu
has bounded support. Its constrained section is closed. Convexity
follows by mixing feasible functions. Every point of M_t(j) lies in
the actual fiber C_j, because (j,x) is the centroid of a positive
measure supported in the convex body C.

For u in R^d its support function has the exact formula

 t h_(M_t(j))(u)
  =inf_(a in R^n,b in R)
       [t b+integral (u.x+a.r_z-b)_+ dmu].                 (6)

The infimum in (6) is not asserted to be attained at every boundary
mass t. The primal support maximum is attained, while dual equality
holds even when no minimizing pair (a,b) exists.

Here is a proof of equality which does not require a constraint
qualification. Let A be the compact convex set of pairs

 ((integral r_z f, integral f), integral u.x f), 0<=f<=1.

At the prescribed constraint c=(0,t), its maximum last coordinate is
v_*=t h_M(u). The point (c,v_*+epsilon) is outside A. Strict separation
from A gives a functional (lambda,eta) whose coefficient eta on the
last coordinate is positive: comparison with the feasible point
(c,v_*) forces eta epsilon>0. Normalize eta=1. Then

 sup_A [lambda.constraint+last coordinate]
       <lambda.c+v_*+epsilon.

Pointwise maximization over 0<=f<=1 evaluates the left side as an
integral of a positive part. Writing lambda=(a,-b) gives a feasible
dual expression in (6) below v_*+epsilon. The reverse weak-duality
inequality follows from (u.x+a.r-b)f<=(u.x+a.r-b)_+.
Let epsilon decrease to zero. This proves (6). The same argument with
only the zero base-moment constraint proves (2).

Thus h_M is genuinely sublinear, unlike an arbitrary directional
quantile map. Its common underlying point set consists only of actual
points of C_j.

## 3. What integration of optimized directional capacities loses

For u!=0 define

 V_u(s)=inf_a mu{u.x+a.r_z>=s}.                            (7)

It is nonincreasing and Lipschitz in s. Bounded section volumes give
a common Lipschitz constant for all cap functions before taking the
infimum. Furthermore V_u is zero for sufficiently large s and equals
D_j for all sufficiently negative s.

For the latter assertion choose U with |u.x|<=U on all fibers. If
s<-U, the fibers satisfying a.r_z>=s+U are completely included in the
cap, and their base halfspace contains j. Thus every cap has mass at
least D_j. Conversely choose a minimizing base halfspace in the form
a_0.r_z>=-1. Replacing a_0 by (1-epsilon)a_0 if necessary leaves its
selected subset unchanged and puts every base point strictly away
from its boundary. For sufficiently negative s the tilt a=(-s)a_0
then includes precisely those whole fibers and excludes all others.
This proves the claimed constant lower-threshold plateau.

Consequently V_u is the survival function of a compactly supported
one-dimensional measure of mass D_j. For 0<t<=D_j define its upper
trimmed-mean functional

 J_t(u)=(1/t) inf_b [t b+integral_b^infinity V_u(s)ds].     (8)

The usual threshold exchange inequality proves that (8) is the mean
of its upper submeasure of mass t. At t=D_j it is simply the full mean
of the directional capacity law.

For each fixed a, Cavalieri and (7) give

 integral (u.x+a.r_z-b)_+ dmu
   =integral_b^infinity mu{u.x+a.r_z>=s}ds
   >=integral_b^infinity V_u(s)ds.

Using (6) therefore proves the exact comparison

 h_(M_t(j))(u)>=J_t(u).                                   (9)

The inequality is caused by one common integer tilt on the left,
whereas the infimum defining V_u can use a different tilt at each
threshold s. There is no equality theorem implicit in (9), and
sublinearity of h_M does not establish sublinearity of J_t.

## 4. Exact strict gap with equal fibers and sharp midpoint domination

Take n=d=1, C=[-1,1] x [0,1], j=0, u=1. The integer fibers are three
identical unit intervals, M=3, D_j=2. For t=2, the support-maximizing
submeasure in (5) is the upper interval [1/3,1] in each fiber. It has
total mass two and zero base moment. The elementary upper-threshold
exchange inequality also makes it optimal among ALL submeasures of
mass two, even without the base constraint. Thus

 h_(M_2(0))(1)=2/3.                                       (10)

The ordinary interval tail is F(s)=min(1,(1-s)_+). Direct endpoint
tilt minimization gives

 inf_a [F(s+a)+F(s-a)]=min(1,2(1-s)_+).

If one cap is full the sum is at least one; otherwise convexity of
the positive part gives at least 2(1-s)_+. Zero tilt or a sufficiently
large finite tilt attains the asserted minimum. Therefore

 V_1(s)=2                 for s<=0,
       =2-s               for 0<=s<=1/2,
       =3(1-s)            for 1/2<=s<=1,
       =0                 for s>=1.

Its measure has mass two and mean

 J_2(1)=(1/2) integral_0^1 V_1(s)ds
       =(1/2)(7/8+3/8)=5/8.                             (11)

The exact strict gap in (9) is therefore 1/24. The endpoint volumes
are equal, the endpoint bodies are identical, and their diagonal
midpoint coupling is uniform on that same interval with density one.
Thus any proposed estimate of this compatibility gap which vanishes
merely under equal endpoint volumes and lossless midpoint-density
domination is false. This example does not contradict OC.

## 5. The regular curvature identity retains the integer coordinates

There is a further exact cross-direction identity. Suppose a support
maximizer in (6) is represented by an actual cap

 L=u.x+a.r_z-b>=0,  u!=0,

whose mass is t and whose first base moment is zero. Assume the fiber
sections remain regular in a neighborhood of these parameters, their
coarea moments depend continuously there, and the section matrix G
below is positive definite.
These are explicit hypotheses, not consequences of (6) at every point.

Let q(z)=(r_z,1), and use the actual coarea section measure

 dnu=(1/|u|) sum_(z in P) dH_(d-1)|_(C_z intersect {L=0}).

Set

 G=integral q q^T dnu,
 B=integral q x^T dnu,
 E=integral x x^T dnu.                                    (12)

Then in a neighborhood of this direction the support function is C^2
and its Hessian is

 Hess h_(M_t(j))(u)=(1/t)[E-B^T G^(-1)B].                 (13)

To verify it, write theta=(a,-b), so L=u.x+theta.q. The exact cap
constraints are integral q 1_{L>=0}dmu=(0,t). Their differential is

 B delta u+G delta theta=0.

Invertibility of G and the ordinary implicit-function theorem give
delta theta=-G^(-1)B delta u and a local C^1 choice of the parameters.
The resulting cap remains a support maximizer: for every feasible f,
the pointwise threshold exchange inequality
(u.x+theta.q)(1_H-f)>=0 has zero constraint contribution after
integration. Moreover grad h_M(u)=t^(-1)integral x 1_H dmu: when
differentiating the support value, the boundary term containing u.x
equals the negative of the term containing theta.q, since L=0 there,
and the latter vanishes by the differentiated constraints. Differentiating
this continuous first moment now gives exactly (13).

Equivalently, for every v in R^d,

 t v^T Hess h_M(u)v
   =min_c integral (v.x+c.q)^2 dnu>=0.                  (14)

This is the squared residual after optimally subtracting an affine
function of the integer base from the continuous coordinate on the
section. It keeps both integer first moments and their covariance;
it is not the unconstrained ordinary moment-body formula. The
homogeneous normal direction is in its nullspace because L=0 on the
section.

## 6. The entire common moment body need not lie in the OC depth region

The common moment body is a candidate domain, not a domain every point
of which is automatically deep. This fails exactly in the simplex-fiber
example from `candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`.
Use its relative volume units, meaning the common reference measure
dx/|B| on EVERY fiber in this paragraph: the fibers A,B,C have masses a,1,1,
where A=(2-q)D, C=qD, (A+C)/2=D subset B, and 0<a<10^(-5).
The anchor is j=0 and its marginal capacity is D_0=1+a.

Let eta be a times uniform probability on D. Its density relative to
that normalized reference is a/(|D|/|B|)=(2-q)^5<1, so eta<=1_B.
Let sigma be a times
uniform probability on C, also dominated by 1_C. Form the actual source
submeasure with its three fiber components

 1_A,       1_B-eta,       sigma.

They are all nonnegative and dominated by their original fibers. Their
masses are a,1-a,a, so they have total D_0 and base mean zero. Their
combined continuous moment is

 a g_A+(g_B-a g_D)+a g_C
      =g_B+a g_D,

because (g_A+g_C)/2=g_D. Consequently

 y_mix=(g_B+a g_D)/(1+a) belongs to M_(D_0)(0).       (15)

The exact cap H_1 in that example contains y_mix and has mass strictly
below gamma_5 M/2, as verified in
`candidate a26d4b26fb2a803f`, section 4.
Thus containment of the WHOLE moment body M_(D_0)(0) in the OC depth
region is false even for three positive, nonheavy simplex fibers.
This does not refute selecting a suitable point of that common body;
no such all-direction existence assertion is made here.

## 7. Exact scope of the new compatibility information

Equations (4)-(6) provide an attained common convex body inside the
selected integer fiber at every mass up to its marginal halfspace
capacity. Equations (13)-(14) provide a common support-curvature
identity when the stated regularity and rank hypotheses hold. The
body therefore supplies real cross-direction compatibility.

What is not proved is an inequality placing an appropriate point of
this body in the Wulff intersection of the optimized cap quantiles at
the OC target. Inequality (9) goes in only one direction, and the
strict product gap (10)-(11) prevents replacing it by equality even
under perfect endpoint midpoint geometry. The arbitrary dominated-
submeasure Jensen theorem in
`candidate cc3ccb4ae42e99f5` applies to
each represented center, but its fiber-mass-dependent constant is not
the desired uniform OC budget. No step here interchanges quantile
optimization and integration or treats different directional laws as
one common measure.
